headline: Morning Signal — QA edition (agentic QA, test tooling, mobile/device debugging, resilience testing)

top_signal.title: Remediate Code Quality findings with agentic autofix
top_signal.summary: GitHub added 'agentic autofix' to Code Quality: you can select up to 25 findings and assign them to Copilot, which applies fixes on a branch, self-validates changes, then opens a pull request under your existing enterprise policy.
top_signal.why_it_matters: Automated bulk fixes change remediation workflows — QA must add PR verification, CI gates, and test-coverage checks to catch regressions from agentic fixes.

items.title: Introducing ADB Wi‑Fi 2.0: faster, more reliable wireless debugging
items.summary: Android published ADB Wi‑Fi 2.0: reworked adb server, adbd daemon, and Android Studio discoverability. Google reports ~32% higher auto‑connection success and 66% faster connections for 90% of sessions.
items.why_it_matters: Improves wireless device stability for local and CI device labs, reducing flaky device connections and setup time for mobile test runs and exploratory debugging.

items.title: Testing application resilience with Amazon SQS and AWS Fault Injection Service
items.summary: AWS published a hands‑on guide and reusable FIS+SSM Automation templates to simulate progressive SQS access loss, define hypotheses, stop conditions, and observability metrics for producer/consumer behavior.
items.why_it_matters: Provides a repeatable resilience experiment and metrics model QA teams can adapt to validate retry logic, circuit breakers, DLQs, and stop‑condition safety for production tests.

items.title: CodeQL 2.27.0 adds support for Linux ARM64
items.summary: CodeQL 2.27.0 is available on Linux ARM64, adds a new Rust security query, expanded Java/Kotlin and C# framework modelling, and accuracy improvements; per‑platform CLI assets provided.
items.why_it_matters: Native ARM64 code scanning lets QA run CodeQL on ARM CI runners and devices without emulation, improving scan coverage and reducing cross‑platform analysis friction.

items.title: Enterprise managed permissions for GitHub Copilot agent operations
items.summary: GitHub added enterprise‑managed permissions to centrally block, require approval for, or allow specific Copilot agent operations (shell commands, file reads/edits, network domains) across app, CLI, and VS Code Agent Host.
items.why_it_matters: Allows QA and platform teams to enforce guardrails for agentic autofix and test agents, control risky operations, and require approvals for changes touching tests, infra, or secrets.

items.title: GitHub Advanced Security expands trial availability
items.summary: GitHub expanded self‑serve GitHub Advanced Security trials from enterprises with up to 100 licenses to enterprises with up to 300 licenses, easing evaluation of Code Security and Secret Protection.
items.why_it_matters: Eases piloting of code scanning and secret-detection across larger QA organizations, useful for validating security gates and scanning workflows before wide rollout.
